change: Observe archive publication batches and cut/coverage outcomes without policy changes; boundary-only VM CPU counters.

cohort.label: candidate
cohort.method: Archive publication/coverage observation with fixed counters, batch-duration histogram and boundary-only VM CPU snapshots. Runtime policy unchanged from archive-cursor bd33ce8; historical reference is not a fresh matched control. Three pinned 1-vCPU/3-GiB nodes, 500 leaders and 1000 followers each, 1500 three-voter groups, four SQL workers/64 reservations, four archive-cut slots, 256-MiB archive budget, 4096-entry cap, 500-ms ticks and 24 writers in two 180-second windows. Fresh persistent internal node and external RustFS backing after cold benchmark VM restart. Quorum/image proofs unchanged. No timed mutation retries; exact 4500 replica values and 1500 archive positions verified. All images, volumes and raw outcomes retained. No builds, profiling or preservation by this task during timing. Closed historical evidence was preserved through verified compression and relocation before this observation. Fresh node and RustFS backing are unchanged.

method_limits: Candidate observation; historical reference is not a fresh matched control.
Successful latency excludes refused requests. All timed errors remain failures.
Stage timings overlap and have different operation counts; they are not additive latency components.
No positional joins of sorted latencies and receipts.
Boundary archive lag is not a continuous retained-entry count.
Other host work remains uncontrolled; this task does not build, profile or preserve artifacts during load.
Coverage index distances include protocol entries and are not admission retained-entry counts.
Batch timers include scheduling, shared verifier waiting and all member cuts; they do not isolate disk service time.
Per-vCPU busy time and softirq counts are VM-wide. Different boundary times prevent exact subtraction of container CPU; activity does not by itself prove scheduling causation.
Live counter snapshots can cross an outcome update; they are not atomic conservation proofs.
Refusal issuance spans use each error's own original retry deadline minus the unchanged 300000-ms command horizon; no receipt/latency positional join.
analyzer_repair: First aggregation overmatched an operation-list string and created a tuple key; narrowed to the selected-operation list. A later refusal-span extraction required parsing decimal deadline strings. Neither failed attempt wrote the final output.
